fills.notes: The clause needs a governing verb before “his throne in the light.” In the oldest cosmological register, establishing/setting a throne in Light is the fixed image of order and dominion, not a personal narrative.

After “which” the text calls for the counterpart of the throne: the uttered ordering principle. “and the word” fits both the grammar (“which … which …”) and the substrate logic (throne = rule in ultimates; word = formative decree).
Completes “which he had also uttered …” in a non-institutional, impersonal way. The pairing throne/utterance is correspondential: fixed order below, proceeding breath/word above.
“When that one will be muzzled, they shall …” demands a parallel restraint. In the substrate idiom, binding + silencing are paired acts of constraint on a hostile power before dismemberment.
Joins “cut limb … there is …” into a coordinated sequence (bind/silence → cut → still remains). Minimal restoration consistent with the syntax.

After dismemberment, the teaching commonly notes that something persists: a “root/remnant” of the nature. This matches the correspondential logic (forms can be cut up, but the underlying nature/root can still remain).

assessment: Most gaps are syntactically constrained but not textually anchored by distinctive names or fixed formulae, so restorations are correspondentially guided (throne/word, binding/silencing, dismemberment/root). Exact wording remains somewhat uncertain in the longer lacunae.
